terms.comment: Classically a cone, the figure, and things of that shape (a helmet’s crest, a cypress cone). Its use for an ice-cream cone is modern, and ours; no reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for it.

terms.gloss: a little ball, a lump of food: a scoop of ice cream
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a little ball … esp. a lump of food, dumpling”. Its use for a scoop of ice cream is ours. The scoop as a tool is Morgan–Owens’s trulla nivāria.

phrases.latin: Vīsne gelātum in cōnō an in catillō?
phrases.english: Do you want your ice cream in a cone or in a cup?
Two scoops in a cone, please.

sources: Lewis & Short: conus · Lewis & Short: globulus · Lewis & Short: trulla
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. ice cream scoop.
